title: Citrix Session Watermarking Enforcement Errors
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Citrix Session Watermarking Enforcement Errors' only. Does not supplant organization-wide SIEM playbooks for unrelated threat classes or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `soc_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `security_infra_citrix_session_watermarking_enforcement_errors` (UC-10.6.198), SOC dashboard panel "Security Infra — Citrix Session Watermarking Enforcement Errors", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:soc_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=xd` sourcetype='citrix:hdx:policy' where `_time` satisfies `err` > 0 for UC-10.6.198 ('Citrix Session Watermarking Enforcement Errors'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `xd` / `citrix:hdx:policy` events where `_time` stays below `err` > 0, or exclude the test entity via `soc_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-10.6.198.

dataSources: `index=xd` `sourcetype="citrix:hdx:policy"` (watermark, screen capture, recording policy apply); `sourcetype="citrix:session:recording:control"` (recording and screenshot rules); VDA and broker events indicating policy not applied or client mismatch Note: field names in SPL are suggested conventions for custom ingestion; actual field names depend on your parsing configuration in props.conf/transforms.conf. Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: No official Splunk TA for HDX policy telemetry. Ingest via Windows Event Logs from VDAs (Session Recording event detection policies log clipboard and file transfer actions), or use Citrix Analytics for Security which surfaces DLP-related risk indicators. Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows for event log collection. — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=xd (sourcetype="citrix:hdx:policy" OR sourcetype="citrix:session:recording:control") earliest=-24h
| eval wm_fail=if(match(_raw, "(?i)watermark.?(fail|error|not.?(applied|enforced))"),1,0), cap_fail=if(match(_raw, "(?i)screen(shot|.?capture).*(deny|block|violation|not.?(allowed|permitted))"),1,0), pol=coalesce(policy_name, policy_set, "unknown")
| where wm_fail=1 OR cap_fail=1
| bin _time span=1h
| stats count as err, values(host) as vda, values(pol) as policies by _time, user, session_id
| where err>0
| table _time, user, session_id, vda, err, policies
description: Watermarking and screen-capture policy protect regulated data in virtual sessions. When the policy stack fails to apply, sessions may run without visible traceability, violating policy intent. Spikes in enforcement errors after image updates, agent upgrades, or client releases warrant rollback or targeted patching before auditors find a gap in technical controls.
value: Early 'Citrix Session Watermarking Enforcement Errors' detection reduces missed threat campaigns, control regressions, and SOC SLA breaches by giving Security Infra operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.
implementation: Correlate errors with a version lookup for Workspace app and VDA. Prioritize high-sensitivity delivery groups. For Session Recording, watch storage and service health in a related availability use case. If errors reference unknown clients, treat as a compliance gap and block out-of-revision clients at the gateway where policy allows.
visualization: Timechart: enforcement errors; table: by `policy_name` and VDA build; list: example raw messages for the support team.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `xd`** — Planned work for 'Citrix Session Watermarking Enforcement Errors' shifts `values` over `span=1h` while `_time` remains in-scope for UC-10.6.198. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `values` on `citrix:hdx:policy`** — Scheduled automation elevates `user` without crossing `err` > 0. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `_time`** — Health checks in `xd` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `citrix:hdx:policy`** — First 48h baseline for `_time` is unstable; window via `soc_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `soc_exception_register.csv` keyed on `_time`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• `index=xd`; `citrix:hdx:policy` and `citrix:session:recording:control` in Splunk; stable `user`+`session_id` for triage. Retain hot data long enough for audit (e.g. 90d).

Step 1 — Configure data collection
`props.conf`/`REPORT-` to extract `policy_name` if embedded in `_raw`. After image or VDA change, log one forced failure and one success; tune regexes to those strings. Tag delivery groups: lookup `sensitive_dg` for alert routing.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Sev-2: `err>0` in 1h for DGs in `sensitive_dg`. Post-upgrade: 24h watch with `quantity=1` on first hit. Throttle: same `user+session_id` 15m. Add panel: timechart of `wm_fail` vs `cap_fail` split by `pol`.

Step 3 — Validate
Reconcile event count to Director policy results or a VDA test session. False positives: compare to DaaS health subsystems vs real `wm_fail=1`.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Monthly compliance PDF: sample raw with policy ID. Escalation: L2 EUC (rollback); L3 TAC with VDA+Workspace build. RFO: attach Splunk time window for regulated apps. Pair with session-recording health use case.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (No official Splunk TA for HDX policy telemetry. Ingest via Windows Event Logs from VDAs (Session Recording event detection policies log clipboard and file transfer actions), or use Citrix Analytics for Security which surfaces DLP-related risk indicators. Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows for event log collection. — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=citrix:hdx:policy, citrix:session:recording:control into xd. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`_time, err, session_id, user`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: We look for the moment the “name-stamped screen” and “no sneaky screen shots” rules fail to take hold — so you are not left telling auditors the protection was on when it quietly was not.
